title: The Dyson Sphere and Dyson Swarm
summary: Freeman Dyson (1960) noted a civilization could capture a star's full output with orbiting collectors; a rigid sphere is unstable, so the realistic form is a swarm of independent habitats and collectors.
body:
Astroengineering studies structures at stellar scale: Dyson swarms, ringworlds, and star-lifting. Freeman Dyson's 1960 paper made it science; the physics is real even where the engineering is distant.

Freeman Dyson (1960) noted a civilization could capture a star's full output with orbiting collectors; a rigid sphere is unstable, so the realistic form is a swarm of independent habitats and collectors. Waste heat would glow in infrared — a technosignature astronomers actually search for.

title: The Kardashev Scale
summary: Nikolai Kardashev (1964) classified civilizations by energy use: Type I (planetary, ~10^16 W), Type II (stellar, ~10^26 W), Type III (galactic, ~10^36 W).
body:
Nikolai Kardashev (1964) classified civilizations by energy use: Type I (planetary, ~10^16 W), Type II (stellar, ~10^26 W), Type III (galactic, ~10^36 W). Humanity is ~0.7 — not yet Type I. Carl Sagan interpolated the scale logarithmically.

title: Orbital Mechanics Calculator
summary: Hohmann transfer math — the same equations that would position megastructure components.
body:

# Hohmann transfer: Earth to Mars (circular, coplanar approximation)
import math
AU = 149597870.7  # km
MU_SUN = 1.32712440018e11  # km^3/s^2
r1, r2 = AU, 1.524*AU
a = (r1+r2)/2
dv1 = math.sqrt(MU_SUN/r1)*(math.sqrt(2*r2/(r1+r2))-1)
dv2 = math.sqrt(MU_SUN/r2)*(1-math.sqrt(2*r1/(r1+r2)))
tof = math.pi*math.sqrt(a**3/MU_SUN)/86400
print(f"delta-v1: {dv1:.2f} km/s, delta-v2: {dv2:.2f} km/s")
print(f"transfer time: {tof:.0f} days")
